x: The Tibetan Plateau is the highest and largest plateau. The Pamir is the "Roof of the World" knot, and the Deccan and Patagonia are much lower.
t: Recall the record each plateau holds.

x: Both are true and R explains A: recent compression folded the rocks, and erosion has not yet worn them down, so the ranges stay high and sharp.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: the Deccan Plateau is built of basaltic lava, and the Chotanagpur Plateau is mineral-rich and drained by the Damodar.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: I, II and III are correct: rivers cut V-shaped valleys, glaciers U-shaped ones and tributary glaciers leave hanging valleys. IV is false because a blind valley is a karst feature.
t: Recall the agent behind each valley.

x: The Himalayas are young fold, the Aravallis old fold, the Sierra Nevada a block mountain and Kilimanjaro volcanic, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall an example of each mountain type.

x: The Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys between faulted blocks. The other pairs are coasts or ordinary river valleys.
t: Recall the rift-valley rivers of India.

x: Both are true and R explains A: sediment piling up at the mouth splits the river into distributaries and builds the delta.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Three come from running water: delta, meander and alluvial fan. A cirque is glacial.
t: Discriminate fluvial from glacial landforms.

x: A cirque is a bowl-shaped hollow, an arête a knife-edged ridge, a horn a sharp pyramidal peak and a moraine glacial debris, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the shape of each glacial landform.

x: Both are true: a barchan is a crescent dune and a seif a long narrow dune parallel to the wind.
t: Discriminate types of dunes.

x: A stalagmite rises from the cave floor; a stalactite hangs from the roof. Lapiaz and dolines are surface karst features.
t: Discriminate stalagmite from stalactite.

x: I, II and III are correct. IV is false because India's eastern coastal plain is broader than the western.
t: Discriminate eastern from western coastal plains.

x: A yardang is a streamlined wind-cut ridge, a mushroom rock is narrow below and wide above, a playa a dry lake bed and loess fine silt, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the features of desert landforms.

x: Both are true and R explains A: the central block sinks between faults as the crust pulls apart, forming the long depression.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: A tombolo is a sand bar joining an island to the mainland. A spit is attached at only one end.
t: Discriminate tombolo from spit.

x: Three are block mountains: Sierra Nevada, Vosges and Black Forest. Fuji is a volcanic mountain.
t: Discriminate block from volcanic mountains.

x: Malwa lies between the Aravalli and Vindhya, Chotanagpur is mineral-rich on the Damodar, Dandakaranya is in the central-eastern highland and Bhander is part of the Vindhyan scarpland, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the location of each Indian plateau.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: being a karst feature does not explain why a stalactite hangs from the roof; dripping water deposits it there.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Waves cut cliffs, caves form in weak zones, caves enlarge through a headland into arches and arches collapse into stacks, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the stages of coastal erosion.

x: The Andes, about 7,000 km long, are the longest mountain range. The Himalayas are the highest.
t: Discriminate longest from highest.

x: Mountains form by folding, faulting, volcanism and erosion. Deposition and marine processes form plains.
t: Recall the processes behind each landform.

x: All six appear in the list of major mountains: Himalayas, Andes, Alps, Rockies, Sierra Nevada and Aravallis.
t: Count each listed item carefully.

x: All six are correct: plateaus form by uplift, volcanism, erosion and deposition, and the Tibetan, Deccan, Pamir, Patagonia and Meseta are major ones.
t: Recall the examples of plateaus.

x: Both are true: plains form by deposition, erosion and marine action, and the Indo-Gangetic Plain and Great Plains are examples.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Valleys are carved by rivers, glaciers, tectonic faulting and karst solution.
t: Recall the processes behind each landform.

x: The key counts all five valley types. Strictly, only the V-shaped valley is a river landform: U-shaped and hanging valleys are glacial, the rift valley tectonic and the blind valley karst.
t: Recall the agent behind each valley.

x: Both are true and R explains A: arêtes, horns, U-shaped and hanging valleys and moraines all come from glacial erosion and deposition.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: R lists examples, while A states the process; examples do not explain the cause.
t: Check whether R is the cause or only examples.

x: Dunes are heaps of sand, yardangs streamlined ridges, mushroom rocks narrow-based and playas dry lake beds, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Recall the features of desert landforms.

x: Loess is wind-blown silt deposited in and around deserts. Stalagmites are karst, beaches coastal and hanging valleys glacial.
t: Discriminate desert landforms from others.

x: All six are karst landforms: sinkholes, dolines, caves, stalactites, stalagmites and blind valleys.
t: Recall the karst landforms.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: listing coastal landforms does not explain that waves, currents and tides make them.
t: Check whether R is the cause or only examples.

x: Both are true: spits and lagoons are coastal landforms; a spit can enclose a lagoon.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All four are correct: tectonic landforms such as rift valleys, horsts, grabens and fold mountains come from faulting, folding and crustal movement.
t: Recall the tectonic landforms.

x: The Alps, Andes and Rockies are all young fold mountains. The Appalachians, Urals, Pennines and Aravallis are old.
t: Discriminate young from old fold mountains.

x: All four are correct: old fold mountains come from ancient folding and long denudation, so they are lower, rounded and highly eroded.
t: Recall the features of old fold mountains.

x: Both are true: volcanic mountains build up from lava and ash into conical peaks.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Residual mountains are what remains when erosion removes softer rock and leaves resistant rock. The other options describe volcanic, block and old fold mountains.
t: Recall the processes behind each mountain type.

x: Residual mountains are remnants of older surfaces, the Appalachians and Pennines are residual mountains and dome mountains form where magma pushes up without erupting. The code pairs items in order when List-II repeats, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall an example of each mountain type.

x: All three are correct: dome mountains are dome-shaped uplifts, as in the Black Hills and Bighorns.
t: Recall an example of each mountain type.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: naming two young fold regions does not explain why the highest peaks occur in young fold belts.
t: Check whether R is the cause or only examples.

x: Both are true: the Appalachians and Aravallis are old fold or residual mountains, and the Sierra Nevada is a block mountain.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All three are correct: the Vosges and Rhine Valley are a block–rift system, Kilimanjaro is volcanic, and the Andes and Himalayas are young fold mountains.
t: Recall an example of each mountain type.

x: All three are correct: compression makes fold mountains, faulting block mountains and volcanism volcanic mountains.
t: Recall the force behind each mountain type.

x: All three are correct: folding forms fold mountains, uplift and downthrow form block mountains and lava accumulation forms volcanic mountains.
t: Recall the process behind each mountain type.

x: Volcanic mountains are typically cones. Fold belts, parallel ranges and fault scarps belong to other types.
t: Recall the shape of each mountain type.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: craters of volcanic mountains have nothing to do with fold mountains having fold belts.
t: Check whether R is even about A.

x: All four are correct: the Himalayas, Alps and Andes are fold mountains and the Sierra Nevada is a block mountain.
t: Recall an example of each mountain type.

x: Tibet is an intermontane plateau, the Piedmont of the USA a piedmont plateau, Africa a continental plateau and the Columbia a lava plateau, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall an example of each plateau type.

x: All four are correct: the Pamir and the Andean plateaus of Bolivia, Peru and Colombia are intermontane plateaus enclosed by ranges.
t: Recall an example of each plateau type.

x: Patagonia is a piedmont plateau at the foot of the Andes. The Pamir is intermontane and Arabia continental.
t: Recall an example of each plateau type.

x: All four are continental plateaus: the Peninsular (Indian), Arabian and Australian plateaus.
t: Recall an example of each plateau type.

x: Both are true: parts of Brazil and Siberia have lava plateaus.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true and R explains A: rivers deposit layer on layer of sediment that builds the fluvial plateau.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All four are fluvial plateaus: Panna, Bhander, Rewa and Rohtas of the Vindhyan region.
t: Recall an example of each plateau type.

x: Both are true: domed plateaus are broad dome-like uplifts, such as the Ozark Plateau.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Tibet covers about 2.5 million km², the Pamir is the Roof of the World, the Meseta lies in the Iberian Peninsula and Iberia includes Spain, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the record each plateau holds.

x: All five are correct: the stable Peninsular Plateau has the Central Highlands north of the Narmada with Bundelkhand and Baghelkhand, the basaltic Deccan to the south and the detached Meghalaya Plateau.
t: Recall the divisions of the Peninsular Plateau.

x: V-shaped valleys are in the upper river course, rift valleys come from faulting, Death Valley is a rift example and a blind valley ends abruptly, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the features of each valley.

x: Both are true: a gorge is a deep, narrow, steep-sided river valley, and a canyon a much deeper gorge such as the Grand Canyon.
t: Discriminate gorge from canyon.

x: A horst is an uplifted fault block, a graben a down-faulted block, Death Valley is in the USA and the Rhine is a rift valley, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Discriminate horst from graben.

x: Both are true: V-shaped valleys are narrow erosional valleys of young rivers, and gorges are deep narrow valleys cut by vertical erosion.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: A canyon comes from intense long erosion, a waterfall from differential erosion, a meander is a winding course and an oxbow lake forms when a meander is cut off, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Recall how each river landform forms.

x: All three are correct: floodplains, natural levees and alluvial fans all come from river deposition.
t: Recall the depositional river landforms.

x: An estuary is a drowned river mouth where tides mix with fresh water. A delta builds out by deposition.
t: Discriminate estuary from delta.

x: An estuary is a funnel-shaped tidal mouth. A drowned glacial U-valley is a fjord and a streamlined hill a drumlin.
t: Discriminate estuary from fjord.

x: The Ganga–Brahmaputra forms a delta, many Western Ghats rivers end in estuaries, deltas form on shallow coasts and estuaries give deeper navigable channels, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Discriminate estuary from delta.

x: A gorge is a deep narrow valley with steep sides, and a canyon a more deeply eroded gorge with very steep sides. The code pairs items in order when List-I repeats, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Discriminate gorge from canyon.

x: All four are correct: Chisapani is a gorge and the Grand Canyon a canyon; gorges come from river erosion and canyons from prolonged erosion.
t: Recall an example of each river landform.

x: All four are correct: a glacier widens a V-valley into a U-valley, a weaker tributary glacier leaves a hanging valley and a waterfall may drop from it.
t: Recall the features of glacial valleys.

x: Both are true and R explains A: a fjord is a deep, narrow inlet because it is a glacial U-valley drowned by the sea.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All three are correct: drumlins are streamlined oval hills of glacial deposits, and eskers are deposited by meltwater.
t: Count the correct statements carefully.

x: An esker is a long winding ridge of sand and gravel laid by meltwater. A raised river bank is a levee and a large karst depression a polje.
t: Recall the shape of each glacial landform.

x: Both are true and R explains A: wind dropping its sand is what builds the dune.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: wind blowing away loose material lowers the ground into a hollow.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: An uvala is coalesced dolines, a polje a large enclosed depression, a blind valley ends abruptly and a swallow hole is where a stream sinks, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the features of karst landforms.

x: A wave-cut platform is left by cliff retreat, a sea stump is an eroded stack and a beach is sand or shingle, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i.
t: Recall the stages of coastal erosion.

x: All four are correct: alluvial plains such as the Indo-Gangetic come from river deposition, floodplains from floods and deltaic plains such as the Ganga–Brahmaputra from deposition at the mouth.
t: Recall the types of plains.

x: Both are true: coastal plains form by marine and river deposition, as on India's east and west coasts.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true: loess plains are wind-blown silt, best known in China and found in other dry regions.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: lying along glacier margins is their location, not the reason meltwater deposits them.
t: Check whether R is the cause or only a location.

x: Both are true and R explains A: block mountains are uplifted horsts beside sunken grabens.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The South American Plateau is a continental plateau, a broad upland rising from the lowlands or sea.
t: Recall an example of each plateau type.

x: All four are correct: waterfalls are sudden drops, oxbow lakes are crescent-shaped, and estuaries have strong tides and tidal flushing with a single funnel mouth.
t: Recall the features of each river landform.

x: Both are true: two cirques cutting back to back make an arête, and three or more around a peak make a horn.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: A mushroom rock comes from wind abrasion, a playa from evaporation, a dune from wind deposition and a yardang from wind erosion, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall how each desert landform forms.

x: All four are correct: the Himalayas have high relief, landslides and glaciers, the plains contain Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar and Khadar, and the plateau includes Deccan, Malwa and Chotanagpur.
t: Recall the physiographic divisions of India.

x: All seven are correct: the Indian Desert includes the Thar, dunes and the Rann, and the Konkan, Malabar, Northern Circars and Coromandel are coastal plains.
t: Recall the physiographic divisions of India.

x: Both are true: India's islands have volcanic, coral or tectonic origins; Lakshadweep is mainly coral.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Chambal valley is known for ravines and badlands made by gully erosion. Coral islands fit Lakshadweep and salt marsh the Rann.
t: Recall the landform of each region.

x: A mushroom rock comes from wind abrasion, a sea cave from weak zones, an arch from a cave cutting through a headland and a stack from an arch collapsing, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the stages of coastal erosion.

x: I, II and III are correct: Western Ghats rivers are short, swift and end in estuaries, and longshore drift builds spits. IV is false because a tombolo, not a spit, joins an island to the mainland.
t: Discriminate tombolo from spit.

x: Both are true: the Rann of Kutch is a salt marsh that floods in the monsoon and dries into a desert.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: flat-topped plateaus say nothing about why mountains are steep.
t: Check whether R is even about A.

x: Barren Island is India's only active volcano, and Narcondam is dormant, giving a-ii, b-i.
t: Discriminate active from dormant volcanoes.
